toc.title: The Well-Architected Framework and the adoption framework

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CAF: Cloud Adoption Framework; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; RDS: Relational Database Service; DMS: Database Migration Service; SCT: Schema Conversion Tool; KMS: Key Management Service; SSL: Secure Sockets Layer; MGN: Application Migration Service

  • Name the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework and tell them apart
  • Say what the AWS Well-Architected Tool is for
  • Describe the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework and its four business outcomes
  • Match a situation to one of the seven migration strategies
  • Know which AWS services help you discover, plan and carry out a migration

2The Well-Architected Framework and the adoption framework

Running case

Tidewater Plans the Move

  • Tidewater's board has agreed to move the shop to AWS, and wants a plan it can trust
  • The CTO asks how to judge whether the new design is a good one
  • The CFO asks what outcomes the move should deliver for the business
  • The IT lead must decide how to move the web servers, the database and an old email system
  • Your job: choose the frameworks, strategies and services that fit

What Is the Well-Architected Framework?

  • The AWS Well-Architected Framework is a set of design principles, best practices and questions for building cloud workloads
  • It is built on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability
  • AWS compares neglecting a pillar to a weak foundation in a building: the system struggles to meet its goals
  • Following the pillars helps you build stable and efficient systems, and leaves room for the functional side of the design
  • The exam asks you to name the pillars and to tell them apart
Exam tip

Learn the six pillar names, and one phrase to recognize each.

The Six Pillars at a Glance

  • Operational excellence: build correctly, deliver a great customer experience, run and improve operations
  • Security: protect data, systems and assets
  • Reliability: work correctly and consistently when expected
  • Performance efficiency: use resources efficiently, and keep doing so as demand changes
  • Cost optimization: deliver business value at the lowest price point
  • Sustainability: reduce environmental impact, especially energy use

Exam tip

Each pillar answers one question: how to run, protect, keep running, perform, save and sustain.

Operational Excellence and Security

  • Operational excellence is a commitment to build software correctly while delivering a great customer experience
  • Its design principles: perform operations as code, make frequent small reversible changes, refine procedures, anticipate failure and learn from all failures
  • Security is the ability to protect data, systems and assets, using cloud technology to improve security
  • Security work on AWS includes access management, encryption, logging and threat detection (Modules 3 to 5)
Exam tip

Operations as code and learning from failure: operational excellence. Protecting data and systems: security.

Reliability and Performance Efficiency

  • Reliability is the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when expected
  • Its principles: recover automatically from failure, test recovery procedures, scale horizontally, stop guessing capacity and manage change through automation
  • Performance efficiency is using cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, and keeping that efficiency as demand and technology change
  • Its principles: democratize advanced technologies, go global in minutes, use serverless architectures, experiment more often and consider mechanical sympathy
Exam tip

Recover and test: reliability. Serverless, global and experiments: performance efficiency.

Cost Optimization and Sustainability

  • Cost optimization is running systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point
  • Its principles: implement cloud financial management, adopt a consumption model, measure overall efficiency, stop spending on undifferentiated heavy lifting and analyze and attribute expenditure
  • Sustainability focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency
  • Cost and sustainability often point the same way: using fewer resources cuts both the bill and the energy
Exam tip

Consumption model and heavy lifting: cost optimization. Energy and environment: sustainability.

Telling the Pillars Apart

The question mentions Pillar
Recovering automatically, testing recovery, scaling out Reliability
Operations as code, small reversible changes, learning from failures Operational excellence
A consumption model, no undifferentiated heavy lifting Cost optimization
Serverless, experimenting, going global in minutes Performance efficiency
Protecting data, systems and assets Security
Energy use and environmental impact Sustainability
Exam tip

"Go global in minutes" and "stop guessing capacity" appear in more than one place: read what the question is really asking.

The AWS Well-Architected Tool

  • The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a service in the console for reviewing workloads against best practices
  • You answer questions about each pillar and receive an action plan to improve
  • Milestones save a point in time so you can track progress
  • Lenses add best practices for specific kinds of workload, including your own
  • Check AWS's pricing page for cost

Exam tip

Reviewing your design against AWS best practices: the Well-Architected Tool.

The Cloud Adoption Framework: Purpose and Outcomes

  • The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) draws on AWS experience to help organizations transform digitally
  • It identifies the capabilities that underpin a successful cloud transformation
  • Use it to prioritize opportunities, assess cloud readiness and evolve the roadmap
  • Four business outcomes: reduce business risk, improve environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance, grow revenue and increase operational efficiency
Exam tip

The four outcomes to remember: risk, ESG, revenue and efficiency.

CAF Perspectives and Phases

  • Six perspectives group the capabilities: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations
  • Business: cloud investments support business outcomes
  • People: culture, structure, leadership and workforce
  • Governance: orchestrate cloud work to maximize benefit and limit risk
  • Four phases: Envision, Align, Launch and Scale

Exam tip

Perspectives say who and what; phases say when: envision, align, launch, scale.

Benefits of Migrating to AWS

  • Migration moves fixed expense to variable expense and ends the work of running data centers
  • It brings the benefits of Module 1: speed and agility, elasticity, global reach and economies of scale
  • The CAF outcomes add lower risk, better ESG performance, revenue growth and operational efficiency
  • Workloads are easier to optimize or re-architect once they are running in the cloud
  • Choose a strategy for each application, so one project can mix strategies
Exam tip

Benefits of migration repeat the benefits of the cloud: speed, elasticity, global reach, lower cost.

Migration Strategies: The Seven Rs

  • AWS names seven migration strategies, the 7 Rs
  • Choose one for each application
  • For large migrations AWS suggests rehost, relocate or replatform first, then modernize after the move
  • Refactor is the most complex and costly strategy

Exam tip

Read how much change the question allows: none is rehost, some is replatform, a redesign is refactor.

3Migration strategies, services and practice

Rehost, Relocate and Replatform

  • Rehost ("lift and shift"): move the application without changes; users keep being served while servers migrate
  • Relocate: move many servers to the cloud version of the platform, or move instances to another VPC, Region or account; no new hardware and no rewrite
  • Replatform ("lift, tinker and shift"): move and add some optimization, for example a Microsoft SQL Server database to Amazon RDS for SQL Server
  • Rehosting makes it easier to optimize later, because the workload is already on AWS
Exam tip

No changes: rehost. A few changes for a managed service: replatform.

Repurchase, Refactor, Retire and Retain

  • Repurchase ("drop and shop"): replace the application with a different product, often moving from a traditional license to SaaS
  • Refactor (re-architect): change the architecture to use cloud-native features; the most complex and costly strategy
  • Retire: decommission applications with no business value, such as idle or unused ones
  • Retain: keep an application where it is for now, for example for data residency, dependencies or a recent upgrade
Exam tip

Replace with a product: repurchase. Switch it off: retire. Leave it for now: retain.

Database Replication With AWS DMS

  • AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) migrates relational databases, data warehouses, NoSQL databases and other data stores
  • Do a one-time migration, or replicate ongoing changes to keep source and target in sync: this is database replication
  • Moving to a different engine: convert the schema first with DMS Schema Conversion or the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT)
  • Pay as you go; data is encrypted at rest with AWS KMS and in transit with SSL

Exam tip

Move a database and keep it in sync: AWS DMS. Convert schemas between engines: AWS SCT.

Migration Services: Discover, Track, Move Old name [Verify live]

  • AWS Application Discovery Service: collects usage and configuration data about on-premises servers
  • AWS Migration Hub: one place to plan and track migrations
  • AWS Application Migration Service: lift and shift of servers with continuous replication; now named AWS Transform MGN
  • Migration Evaluator: builds a data-driven business case with right-sized cost projections
  • As of 4 November 2026: Discovery Service and Migration Hub are closed to new customers; AWS points to AWS Transform

Exam tip

Find servers: Discovery Service. Track: Migration Hub. Move servers: Application Migration Service. Business case: Migration Evaluator.

What the Exam Asks: Frameworks and Migration

  • Reliability or operational excellence: recover and test, or run and learn
  • Cost optimization or sustainability: lowest price point, or lowest environmental impact
  • Well-Architected Framework or Tool: the guidance, or the review in the console
  • CAF perspectives or phases: the areas, or the stages in time
  • Rehost, replatform or refactor: no change, some change, or a redesign
  • DMS or SCT: move and replicate data, or convert the schema
Exam tip

Name the situation first, then the pillar, strategy or service.

Design Check: Tidewater's Migration Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
Judge whether the new design is a good one Well-Architected Framework and Tool
Agree the business outcomes of the move CAF: risk, ESG, revenue, efficiency
Move the web servers exactly as they are Rehost
Move the database and keep it in sync AWS DMS replication
Replace the old email system Repurchase a SaaS product
An application nobody uses Retire
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

Common Traps: Frameworks and Migration

  • Pillars are not services: the Well-Architected Framework is guidance, not something you launch
  • Tool and Framework differ: the Tool reviews a workload; the Framework holds the pillars
  • Rehost is not replatform: replatform changes something to gain a benefit
  • Refactor is not the fast option: it is the most complex and costly
  • Names move: Application Migration Service is now AWS Transform MGN; older material and questions may use the old name
Exam tip

When a service name looks unfamiliar, think about what the old name did.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which list names the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

  • AOperational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability
  • BSecurity, availability, scalability, speed, support and compliance, each applied to every service
  • CCompute, storage, networking, databases, analytics and machine learning, the main service categories
  • DPlanning, design, build, test, release and maintenance, the phases of a software project
Show the answer

Answer: A. The six pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability. The other lists mix quality words, service categories or project phases that are not the pillars.

S2A team keeps its runbooks as code, makes small reversible changes, and reviews every incident to improve its procedures. Which pillar does this describe?

  • APerformance efficiency
  • BOperational excellence
  • CCost optimization
  • DReliability
Show the answer

Answer: B. Performing operations as code, making frequent small reversible changes and learning from failures are operational excellence principles. Reliability is about recovering and scaling, cost optimization is about price, and performance efficiency is about using resources well.

S3Tidewater wants its shop to recover from failures without manual work. Which TWO practices support the reliability pillar? (Select TWO.)

  • AMonitor key indicators and run automation when a threshold is breached
  • BReplace one large server with several smaller ones that do not share a failure point
  • CMake changes to the infrastructure by hand so that they are fully controlled
  • DSkip recovery tests because testing might cause a failure
  • ERun the whole shop on one very large server to keep things simple
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Automatic recovery from monitored failures and scaling out across several smaller resources are reliability principles. Hand changes, untested recovery and a single large server all raise the risk of failure.

S4Which statement describes the cost optimization pillar?

  • AProtecting data, systems and assets from unauthorized access
  • BUsing cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements as demand and technology change
  • CReducing the environmental impact of workloads
  • DRunning systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point
Show the answer

Answer: D. Cost optimization is about delivering business value at the lowest price point. The other statements describe security, performance efficiency and sustainability.

S5Tidewater wants to review its shop against AWS best practices and receive an improvement plan. Which AWS tool fits?

  • AAWS Artifact, the portal for compliance reports
  • BAWS CloudTrail, the record of account activity
  • CAWS Well-Architected Tool
  • DAmazon Inspector, the scanner for vulnerabilities
Show the answer

Answer: C. The AWS Well-Architected Tool reviews a workload against the framework's best practices and produces an action plan. Artifact provides compliance reports, CloudTrail records account activity and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

S6Which pillar focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency?

  • AReliability
  • BOperational excellence
  • CSecurity
  • DSustainability
Show the answer

Answer: D. The sustainability pillar is about environmental impacts, with energy use and efficiency as the main levers. The other pillars cover recovering from failure, running operations and protecting assets.

S7Which TWO are business outcomes that the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations pursue? (Select TWO.)

  • AReduced business risk
  • BA smaller number of AWS Regions
  • CIncreased operational efficiency
  • DThe removal of all security responsibilities
  • EA fixed hardware refresh cycle
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Reducing business risk and increasing operational efficiency are two of the four CAF outcomes, together with improved ESG performance and revenue growth. The other options are not outcomes the framework describes.

S8Tidewater moves its web servers to AWS exactly as they are, with no changes to the application. Which migration strategy is this?

  • ARehost
  • BRefactor
  • CRepurchase
  • DRetire
Show the answer

Answer: A. Moving an application without changes is rehosting, also called lift and shift. Refactoring redesigns it, repurchasing replaces it with a different product, and retiring switches it off.

S9A company replaces its on-premises email system with a vendor's software-as-a-service product. Which migration strategy is this?

  • AReplatform
  • BRelocate
  • CRepurchase
  • DRetain
Show the answer

Answer: C. Replacing an application with a different product, often SaaS, is repurchasing, sometimes called drop and shop. Replatforming and relocating keep the same application, and retaining leaves it where it is.

S10Tidewater must keep its order database running during the move and keep the copy in the cloud in sync until cutover. Which AWS service fits?

  • AAmazon Athena, the service for querying data
  • BAWS Config, the record of resource settings
  • CAmazon CloudFront, the content delivery service
  • DAWS Database Migration Service
Show the answer

Answer: D. AWS DMS migrates databases and can replicate ongoing changes so that source and target stay in sync. Athena queries data, Config tracks resource configuration and CloudFront delivers content.

S11Which statement about migration strategies is correct?

  • AReplatforming never changes anything about the application, because it only moves its servers as they are
  • BReplatforming changes the application a little to gain a benefit, such as a managed database service
  • CRefactoring is the quickest and least costly strategy, because it needs no redesign of the application
  • DRetiring an application means moving it to another Region and keeping it running there as before
Show the answer

Answer: B. Replatform means moving with some optimization, for example to a managed database service. Refactoring is the most complex and costly strategy, and retiring means decommissioning an application.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Well-Architected pillars operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability
Telling them apart operations as code, protect, recover and test, serverless and experiments, consumption model, environmental impact
Tool reviews a workload against best practices and gives an action plan with milestones
CAF six perspectives, four phases, four outcomes: risk, ESG, revenue, efficiency
Seven Rs retire, retain, rehost, relocate, replatform, repurchase, refactor
Services DMS replicates databases, Application Migration Service moves servers, Migration Evaluator builds the case
